title: Smith Machine Hip Thrust
summary: A hip thrust on a fixed bar path, which is easier to set up than with a barbell.

equipment_needs.text: Needs: Smith machine; weight plates; flat bench.

muscles.why: Library rating 1 for glutes (main mover): each working set adds 1 of a set to the weekly glutes total.
Library rating 0.4 for hamstrings (helper): each working set adds 0.4 of a set to the weekly hamstrings total.
Library rating 0.3 for abductors (minor): each working set adds 0.3 of a set to the weekly abductors total.
Library rating 0.2 for quads: below the counting floor, so it adds nothing to the weekly quads total.

setup.text: Sit with your upper back against a bench and the padded bar across your hips.
Plant your feet flat, about hip width apart.
Drive your hips up until your body is straight from knees to shoulders.
Squeeze your glutes at the top, then lower under control.

form_cues.cue: Keep your chin tucked and ribs down so the glutes, not your lower back, finish the rep.

mistakes.text: Pushing through the toes instead of the heels.

lower_risk.text: Warm-up: the app adds two or three ramp-up sets at rising loads before the first working set, unless that load is very light.
The app suggests a heavier load only when the jump is 5% or less; otherwise it adds a rep first.
Default target: 6-10 reps, stopping about 3 reps short of failure (RIR 3). Stop the set when form breaks down.
Use the same controlled range on every rep; lower under control rather than dropping or bouncing.
Set safety arms or pins where you can fail a rep safely, or use a spotter, and use collars.
Pick a variation and range you can train pain-free.
